item_taken.first_six_words: Stops on its best: a striking
item_taken.why: The case is the item's own carrier restated: a breath whose finish condition is a new member the first framing hid, ended at that member, with a region of one inhabitant, which is the ledger tell the item names, and the case says the stop is Stops on its best; it is not Both ends named (no axis, no endpoints, the stop is on a member not a limit), not Phantom tail (the member it stops on is right, not wrong), and not One role throughout (the reversed half is entered, then left at once).

reasoning: The rule sorts one thing: a named axis. What the axis produces, the limiting members it conscripts at its ends, goes to form-yields; the walk that closes on those ends while the subject stays open stays here; the same axis yields there and stalls here. The case holds no axis and no limiting member. Its stop is made of the enumerator's satisfaction with one striking member, a member that opens a region rather than closing an axis, and the breath's finish condition is a member, not a coordinate. So neither clause of the rule fires: the case is not an axis yield, and it is not a walk closing on axis ends. The rule does not say no (the case stays) because its here-clause is as axis-shaped as its there-clause; it simply does not see the case. The nearest crossing reading, that the first framing is a form and the striking member is what the reversed form made visible, is a reading of form-yields' own definition (a form producing a member the pile did not hold), not of this rule, which names an axis and nothing wider. To decide, the rule would need either a case that holds a named axis with the stopping member at one of its ends, or a rule widened from the axis to any imposed form (a framing, a finish condition) and its produced member. The fence is drawn for Both ends named and reads as a passage; for a case on Stops on its best it is a wall.
